properties.title: Brain Latent Progression: Individual-based Spatiotemporal Disease Progression on 3D Brain MRIs via Latent Diffusion

properties.version_basis: PDF identified by SHA-256 against assignments.json; title page read.

properties.description: Retrospective evaluation of a latent-diffusion model that predicts follow-up 3D brain T1w MRI, with an internal test split of ADNI, OASIS-3 and AIBL and an external NACC test set.
properties.independent_study_claim: authors' own study; external test set from a separate cohort

properties.description: Autoencoder, conditional latent diffusion UNet, ControlNet on baseline latent, auxiliary volume-progression model (linear or Disease Course Mapping), and Latent Average Stabilization.
properties.world_model_status: conditional generative progression model; persistent state across steps absent

properties.algorithm: Brain Latent Progression (latent diffusion with ControlNet, auxiliary progression prior and LAS)
properties.base_model: MONAI pretrained brain latent diffusion autoencoder, fine-tuned

properties.population: cognitively normal, MCI and Alzheimer's disease subjects with baseline T1w MRI
properties.decision: retrospective patient selection for clinical trials is demonstrated; no deployment use is defined

properties.description: Internal test split (15 percent of subjects) of ADNI 1/2/3/GO, OASIS-3 and AIBL; subject count of the split not stated
NACC longitudinal study, 962 subjects, 2,257 T1w MRIs, evaluation only
Held-out subject-level test sets (internal 15 percent split and external NACC) with paired t-tests and Bonferroni correction on some comparisons

relation_assertions.rationale: Prediction of future structural state from a baseline scan and covariates, with no action selection or causal effect claim. Uncertainty is reported but not calibrated, so BP_FORECAST fits better than BP_MULTI.
Reviewer mapping: a learned conditional generator with an auxiliary progression prior. Legacy M3 and M7 are not adopted because no recurrent state service or causal layer is implemented.

capability_assessments.rationale: Core world-model identity (V11) is not met because state.persistent and dynamics.temporal are partial: each target age is generated directly from a baseline latent and auxiliary-model covariates without carrying or updating a persistent clinical state across steps. Consequently, formal capability is downgraded from L1 to not_world_model (evaluated supporting component), while preserving that predicted follow-up MRIs and regional volumes are scored against real follow-up scans on internal and external test sets (rollout.one_step_evaluated present at evaluation).

Core world-model identity (V11) is not met because state.persistent and dynamics.temporal are partial: each target age is generated directly from a baseline latent and auxiliary-model covariates without carrying or updating a persistent clinical state across steps. Consequently, formal capability is downgraded from L1 to not_world_model (evaluated supporting component), while preserving that predicted follow-up MRIs and regional volumes are scored against real follow-up scans on internal and external test sets (rollout.one_step_evaluated present at evaluation).

gate_assessments.rationale: Subject-level splits and an external cohort are stated, but subject overlap across source cohorts, the pretraining data of the autoencoder and use of target-age cognitive status are not addressed.

Predicted follow-up scans and regional volumes are evaluated against real follow-ups on internal and external held-out cohorts (rollout.one_step_evaluated present at evaluation), but G02 requires state.persistent and dynamics.temporal to be present at evaluation, whereas both are partial because generation is direct age-conditioned synthesis from the baseline scan rather than a stepwise persistent-state transition.
Uncertainty is associated with error but calibration or coverage is not evaluated.
An external cohort and subgroups are reported, but only differences between conditioning settings are tested and no shift detection or composition analysis exists.

legacy_cells.B: Brain Latent Progression: Individual-based Spatiotemporal Disease Progression on 3D Brain MRIs via Latent Diffusion
legacy_cells.C: Puglisi, Lemuel, Alexander, Daniel C., Ravì, Daniele
legacy_cells.O: Alzheimer’s disease and age-related brain change in cognitively normal, MCI, and AD groups
legacy_cells.S: Can an individual’s future 3D brain MRI and regional volume progression be forecast from baseline MRI, subject covariates, and optionally prior visits?
legacy_cells.T: Internal ADNI/OASIS-3/AIBL cohort: 2,805 subjects with at least two MRIs at different visits; external NACC cohort: 962 subjects.
legacy_cells.V: Retrospective selection of fast progressors for clinical-trial recruitment.
legacy_cells.AI: 3D T1-weighted brain MRI; age, sex, cognitive status; regional brain-volume progression covariates (including hippocampus, cortex, amygdala, cerebral white matter, and lateral ventricles)
legacy_cells.AJ: MRI autoencoder; conditional UNet latent diffusion model; ControlNet; auxiliary regression model or Disease Course Mapping (DCM); Latent Average Stabilization (LAS)
legacy_cells.BA: LAS repeats stochastic inference m times and averages latent predictions to stabilize spatiotemporal progression.
legacy_cells.BN: Auxiliary disease-progression prior: regression for single-scan input or logistic Disease Course Mapping (DCM) adjusted to the subject’s observed longitudinal regional-volume history.
legacy_cells.BS: Predicted future 3D brain MRI; global scalar and voxel-level uncertainty estimates/maps.
legacy_cells.BV: Latent diffusion noise-prediction loss Lε; ControlNet is trained using the same loss.
legacy_cells.CG: LAS repeats inference m times; m = 64 was used for experiments unless otherwise specified.
legacy_cells.DQ: Internal: 11,730 T1w MRI scans from 2,805 subjects; external: 2,257 T1w MRI scans from 962 subjects.
legacy_cells.DX: Compared with baselines on external test data, BrLP achieved 60.23% average MSE reduction and 22.84% average SSIM increase; volumetric improvements were also reported.
legacy_cells.EC: Retrospective fast-progressor selection: BrLP identified 24.94% more fast progressors than random selection internally and 23.85% more externally.
legacy_cells.EK: Ablations varied LAS sample count m; removed/added the auxiliary progression model and LAS; tested incorrect cognitive-status conditioning; and varied DDIM denoising steps.
legacy_cells.EL: Authors report lower accuracy for AD than healthy-aging cases, possible sex-related performance bias, and output smoothing that may remove fine-grained detail.
legacy_cells.FB: 3D MRI encoded into a compact continuous latent tensor and conditioned on subject metadata plus progression-related regional volumes.
legacy_cells.FL: Autoencoder encodes baseline 3D MRI to a compact latent; an auxiliary regression/DCM model predicts target regional volumes; conditional latent diffusion with ControlNet generates a target-age latent using the baseline latent and covariates; decoder produces the future MRI; LAS averages repeated generations and estimates uncertainty. No planner is implemented.
legacy_cells.FM: BrLP combines latent diffusion and ControlNet for individualized 3D MRI progression, an auxiliary model for longitudinal disease-progression priors, and LAS for spatiotemporal stabilization and uncertainty estimation.
legacy_cells.FN: On external test data, BrLP reported 60.23% average MSE reduction and 22.84% average SSIM increase versus baselines. Voxel-level uncertainty correlated with voxel-wise squared error (Spearman 0.63 ± 0.11). Retrospective fast-progressor identification exceeded random selection by 23.85% externally and 24.94% internally.
legacy_cells.FO: Reported limitations: reduced accuracy for AD relative to healthy aging; possible sex-related bias; and VAE-associated smoothing that may reduce fine-grained detail.
legacy_cells.FP: Future work: disentangle disease progression from aging, add disease-specific variables, model cognitive-stage transitions, and evaluate adaptation to other brain diseases and chronic conditions affecting other organs.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors identify challenges in individualization, use of longitudinal data, spatiotemporal consistency, and memory demands of 3D imaging.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence supports retrospective MRI progression forecasting and external-dataset evaluation, not treatment-conditioned or causally identified counterfactual effects, prospective clinical benefit, or deployment. Trial-selection results are retrospective; treatment-effect simulation is described as future potential.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Expose future-state forecasts through a time-aware dynamics interface and validate error versus horizon; treatment actions need separate evidence before intervention simulation.
legacy_cells.FX: Title and abstract (p. 1); introduction and related work (pp. 1–5); methods/background, architecture, inference, uncertainty, implementation and preprocessing (pp. 5–8); datasets, metrics, tables 1–4 and experiments/results (pp. 8–16); discussion and conclusion (p. 16); data availability and acknowledgments (p. 17); appendix auxiliary models, datasets, DDIM analysis and Table 5 (pp. 19–21). | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: The full 21-page extracted text was reviewed. Several tables have flattened/misaligned extracted cell layout, so extraction relies on legible prose results where available. Capability is L1 and clinical readiness R3; conditioning on demographics, MRI history, or cognitive status is not treatment-action conditioning or causal identification. No planner or treatment-effect simulation was evaluated. The schema refers to separate KB module/open-problem mappings, but those mappings were not supplied; FS was therefore omitted. A:I remain untouched. Evidence QA: 61/69 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (88.4%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Schema normalization (source details retained): DU normalized to 'Multiple'; source detail: Internal subjects randomly split 80% training / 5% validation / 15% test, with no subject overlap; external NACC set used solely for evaluation. Codex audit: 62 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 7 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: All 21 PDF pages were read as extracted text. Pages 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 (Figures 1 to 7 and Tables 1 to 4) were rendered at 60 to 80 dpi and viewed by this reviewer. Pages 18 to 21 (References, Appendix A-D, Figure 8 DDIM-step ablation, and Table 5 sex-stratified evaluation) were subsequently visually inspected during Phase E repair; pages 1 to 4, 16, and 17 were read as text only. Full bibliography entries on physical pages 18–19 were subsequently read in the targeted 2026-11-22 local review; cited full studies remain unretrieved.

Only a subset of columns of Tables 1 to 3 (MSE, SSIM, hippocampus and lateral ventricle MAE for all subjects) was transcribed into metrics. Cognitive-status strata, other regions and Table 5 are not transcribed.
No code or repository was inspected. Release statements are author claims.
Core-model status is a reviewer judgement: a different reading of state.persistent could keep the legacy core classification.
Legacy cells were read from the root workbook row (read only). Unlisted columns remain imported-only. Saved API drafts for B022 were not opened.
Schema validity and quote occurrence do not establish semantic correctness. One reviewer pass; no independent human review.
notes: Latent diffusion with ControlNet that generates a follow-up 3D brain MRI from a baseline scan and covariates, with an auxiliary progression prior and repeated-sample averaging that also gives uncertainty. L1 supported by internal and external follow-up comparisons. Not treated as a core world model because no state is carried across steps. Source points: target-age cognitive status as an input, unreported subject overlap across cohorts, unexamined pretraining data, small effects of wrong conditioning, and no uncertainty calibration.
